subproblem.title: A finite set has approximate tangent space {0} in dimension 0 at each of its points
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let F ⊆ ℝ^P be a finite set and let y ∈ F. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y ⊥ holds (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 with n = 0). Explicitly: the zero subspace ⊥ = {0} has dimension 0, and for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ → ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ = f(0) as ρ → 0 with ρ > 0. Here η_{y,ρ}(z) = ρ⁻¹(z − y) is SimonGMT blowUpMap y ρ and H⁰ = μHE[0].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P), F.Finite → y ∈ F → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y ⊥
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 6, orientation at y ∈ F: with δ := dist(y, F ∖ {y}) > 0 and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0), for 0 < ρ < δ/R_f the blow-up ρ⁻¹(F − y) meets tsupport f at most in 0, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y {0}. Simon's printed proof of Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt line 2323) only says that "the theorem is trivial in case n = 0", so this argument is extracted and specialized from the parent-supplied proof of dmcbr_closure_degree_zero (Part III, CL(0)).

Definition used. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y Q (SimonGMT Chapter03; Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) means: finrank Q = 0, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) the function ρ ↦ ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ tends to ∫_Q f dH⁰ along 𝓝[>] 0, where η_{y,ρ}(z) = ρ⁻¹•(z − y) is SimonGMT blowUpMap y ρ and H⁰ = μHE[0]. We take Q = ⊥ = {0}.

1. Dimension. finrank ℝ (⊥ : Submodule ℝ ℝ^P) = 0 (Mathlib finrank_bot). Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
2. Limit value. The carrier of ⊥ is {0} (Submodule.bot_coe), the coercion of the finset {0}. The first identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero (count_integral), applied to the finset {0}, gives ∫_⊥ f dH⁰ = f(0).
3. Support radius. tsupport f is compact (f.hasCompactSupport), hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R₀ := max(R, 0) + 1 > 0. If ‖z‖ ≥ R₀, then ‖z‖ > R, so z ∉ tsupport f and f(z) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
4. Separation radius. F ∖ {y} is finite, hence closed, and does not contain y. Its complement is therefore an open neighbourhood of y, so there is δ > 0 with B_δ(y) ∩ (F ∖ {y}) = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Thus ‖z − y‖ ≥ δ for every z ∈ F with z ≠ y (vacuous if F = {y}).
5. Fix ρ ∈ (0, δ/R₀); this interval belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 because δ/R₀ > 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). The image η_{y,ρ}(F) is finite (Set.Finite.image); regard it as a finset. The first identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero gives ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ = Σ_{w ∈ η_{y,ρ}(F)} f(w).
6. The point η_{y,ρ}(y) = ρ⁻¹•0 = 0 lies in the image, since y ∈ F, and contributes f(0). Every other element w of the image is η_{y,ρ}(z) for some z ∈ F with z ≠ y (if z = y then w = 0). For such w, ‖w‖ = ρ⁻¹‖z − y‖ ≥ ρ⁻¹δ > R₀, because ρR₀ < δ; so f(w) = 0 by step 3. Hence Σ_{w ∈ η_{y,ρ}(F)} f(w) = f(0) (Finset.sum_eq_single 0).
7. By steps 5–6, ρ ↦ ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ equals the constant f(0) on (0, δ/R₀), i.e. eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, so it tends to f(0) (tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_eq), and f(0) = ∫_⊥ f dH⁰ by step 2. Together with step 1 this proves HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y ⊥. ∎

proof_key_steps: finrank ⊥ = 0, and the integral of f over ⊥ = {0} is f(0) (count_integral)
choose R₀ > 0 with f = 0 outside the open ball of radius R₀, and δ > 0 separating y from F ∖ {y}
for 0 < ρ < δ/R₀ the blow-up of F is a finset containing 0 whose other points have norm > R₀, so its integral is f(0) (count_integral, Finset.sum_eq_single)
the integral is eventually the constant f(0) along 𝓝[>] 0, hence converges to the integral over ⊥

subproblem.title: Degree-0 integer multiplicity currents are finite weighted point sums on compactly contained sets
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and U, B ⊆ ℝ^P. Let R be a degree-0 IMRep in U representing S ∈ 𝒟_0(U), and suppose B ⊂⊂ U (closure B is compact and contained in U). Then there are N ∈ ℕ, w : ℕ → ℤ and x : ℕ → ℝ^P such that: x_l ∈ B and w_l ≠ 0 for every l < N; Σ_{l<N} |w_l| ≤ R.measure(B) in [0, ∞]; and S(ω) = Σ_{l<N} w_l ⟨ω(x_l)⟩ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. Here ⟨α⟩ := α(e) is the value of a 0-covector on the empty family e = (fun i => i.elim0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U B : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U 0) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), R.Represents S → CompactlyContained B U → ∃ (N : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℤ) (x : ℕ → Euclid P), (∀ l < N, x l ∈ B) ∧ (∀ l < N, w l ≠ 0) ∧ (∑ l ∈ Finset.range N, ((w l).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞)) ≤ R.measure B ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U 0, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) ⊆ B → S ω = ∑ l ∈ Finset.range N, (w l : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) (x l) (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (i)–(iii) and the per-j listing of step 3. The multiplicity of each point is kept as an integer weight w = εθ instead of listing the point θ times with sign ε, and the mass is recorded through R.measure (the parent converts it to M_B with (MR)). Simon's printed proof of Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt line 2323) only says that "the theorem is trivial in case n = 0", so this argument is extracted and specialized from the parent-supplied proof of dmcbr_closure_degree_zero (Part III, CL(0)).

Notation. M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient. e : Fin 0 → ℝ^P is the empty family (Lean: fun i => i.elim0); every family Fin 0 → ℝ^P equals e (function extensionality over the empty type). Put ⟨α⟩ := α(e) for α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 0). H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and H⁰{p} = 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Let K := closure B; since B ⊂⊂ U, K is compact and K ⊆ U.

1. Local finiteness. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult, I := ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞. Suppose M ∩ K were infinite. Pick n ∈ ℕ with I < n (ENNReal.exists_nat_gt) and an n-element finset F' ⊆ M ∩ K (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq). Since θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos), n = Σ_{x∈F'} 1 ≤ Σ_{x∈F'} θ(x) = ∫⁻_{F'} θ dH⁰ (lower-integral identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ = I (lintegral_mono_set), contradicting I < n. So M ∩ K is finite, and G := M ∩ B ⊆ M ∩ K is finite (B ⊆ closure B). Regard G as a finset.
2. Orientation at every point of M. Let p ∈ M, and suppose no Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M p Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(p)) Q. Let Z be the set of points without such a Q. The field orients says (H⁰⌞M)(Z) = 0 (ae_iff); since {p} ⊆ Z, (H⁰⌞M){p} = 0 (measure_mono_null). But (H⁰⌞M){p} = H⁰({p} ∩ M) = H⁰{p} = 1 (Measure.restrict_apply with the measurable set {p}, and p ∈ M), a contradiction. Hence for each p ∈ M there are Q and τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with either ξ(p)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(p)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (definition of IsUnitOrientationOf). As τ = e, there is ε(p) ∈ {1, −1} ⊆ ℤ with ξ(p)(α) = ε(p)⟨α⟩ for every α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 0). Choose such ε(p) for each p ∈ M, and any value elsewhere.
3. Action. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. Since R represents S, S(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH⁰. For x ∈ M ∖ G we have x ∉ B ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and θ(x)ξ(x)(0) = 0, ξ(x) being linear. subproblem.title: Finite integer combinations of point evaluations are integer multiplicity 0-currents
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and S ∈ 𝒟_0(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V 0). Let M ∈ ℕ, v : ℕ → ℤ and y : ℕ → ℝ^P; the points y_l need not lie in V. Write ⟨α⟩ := α(e) for the value of a 0-covector α on the empty family e : Fin 0 → ℝ^P (Lean: fun i => i.elim0). If S(ω) = Σ_{l<M} v_l ⟨ω(y_l)⟩ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(V), then S is integer multiplicity: some degree-0 IMRep R in V represents S.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V 0) (M : ℕ) (v : ℕ → ℤ) (y : ℕ → Euclid P), (∀ ω : TestFormOn V 0, S ω = ∑ l ∈ Finset.range M, (v l : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0) (y l) (fun i => i.elim0)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5 (cancellation: m(y) := Σ_{i: y_i = y} ε_i and F := {y ∈ Y ∩ B_r(x₀) : m(y) ≠ 0}) and step 6 (explicit IMRep with finite carrier), here stated for an arbitrary domain V and arbitrary integer coefficients. Simon's printed proof of Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt line 2323) only says that "the theorem is trivial in case n = 0", so this argument is extracted and specialized from the parent-supplied proof of dmcbr_closure_degree_zero (Part III, CL(0)).

Notation. e : Fin 0 → ℝ^P is the empty family (Lean: fun i => i.elim0); for a 0-covector α put ⟨α⟩ := α(e). Let ev ∈ MultiVector P 0 be the continuous linear functional α ↦ α(e) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ e), so ev(α) = ⟨α⟩. H⁰ = μHE[0].
1. Cancellation. For p ∈ ℝ^P let m(p) := Σ_{l<M} (if y_l = p then v_l else 0) ∈ ℤ. Let Y := {y_l : l < M} (the finset image of range M under y) and G := {p ∈ Y : p ∈ V and m(p) ≠ 0} (Finset.filter), a finite subset of V.
2. Reduced formula for S. For every φ : ℝ^P → ℝ, Σ_{l<M} v_l φ(y_l) = Σ_{p∈Y} m(p) φ(p): expand m(p) (Int.cast_sum, Int.cast_ite, Finset.sum_mul), exchange the two sums (Finset.sum_comm), and for fixed l keep only the term p = y_l ∈ Y (Finset.sum_eq_single). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(V) and φ(p) := ⟨ω(p)⟩. If p ∈ Y and m(p)⟨ω(p)⟩ ≠ 0, then m(p) ≠ 0 and ω(p) ≠ 0, and the latter gives p ∈ tsupport ω ⊆ V (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So the nonzero terms are indexed by G (Finset.sum_filter_of_ne), and S(ω) = Σ_{p∈G} m(p)⟨ω(p)⟩.
3. The triple. Define carrier := G; mult := the indicator of G applied to p ↦ |m(p)| ∈ ℕ (Int.natAbs); s := the indicator of G applied to p ↦ sign(m(p)) ∈ ℝ (Int.sign, cast to ℝ); orient(p) := s(p)·ev. For p ∈ G we have sign(m(p)) = 1 if m(p) > 0 and sign(m(p)) = −1 if m(p) < 0 (Int.sign_eq_one_of_pos, Int.sign_eq_neg_one_of_neg).
4. IMRep axioms. (a) G is finite, hence measurable (Set.Finite.measurableSet), and G ⊆ V by construction. (b) Rectifiability. If G = ∅, it is H⁰-null, hence countably 0-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero). Otherwise G is countable and nonempty, so G = range φ for some φ : ℕ → ℝ^P (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range). Take M₀ = ∅ and let F_j : ℝ^0 → ℝ^P be the constant map with value φ(j), which is Lipschitz with constant 0 (LipschitzWith.const). Since 0 ∈ ℝ^0, φ(j) ∈ range F_j, so G ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j, i.e. CountablyRectifiable 0 G. (c) Measurability. Each p ↦ (if y_l = p then v_l else 0) is measurable because {p : y_l = p} = {y_l} is measurable (Measurable.ite), so m is measurable as a finite sum (Finset.measurable_sum; ℤ carries the discrete σ-algebra). Every map out of ℤ is measurable (Measurable.of_discrete), so p ↦ |m(p)| and p ↦ sign(m(p)) are measurable, and so are their indicators on the measurable set G (Measurable.indicator). Thus mult and s are measurable, and orient = s(·)·ev is strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable, StronglyMeasurable.smul_const), in particular a.e. strongly measurable for H⁰⌞G. (d) For p ∈ G, mult(p) = |m(p)| ≥ 1 because m(p) ≠ 0 (Int.natAbs_pos). (e) For compact K ⊆ V: ∫⁻_{G∩K} mult dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_G mult dH⁰ (lintegral_mono_set) = Σ_{p∈G} mult(p) < ∞, by the lower-integral identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero (count_integral). (f) Orientation. We prove the property at every p ∈ G, which gives the H⁰⌞G-a.e. statement because G is measurable (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem). Take Q := ⊥. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 G p ⊥ is the sibling theorem dmcbrz_approxTangent_finite_zero (finite_tangent; G is finite and p ∈ G). IsUnitOrientationOf (orient p) ⊥ holds with τ := e: τ is orthonormal vacuously (Fin 0 is empty); span(range e) = span ∅ = ⊥; and orient(p)(α) = sign(m(p))⟨α⟩, which equals α(τ) for all α if m(p) > 0 and −α(τ) for all α if m(p) < 0.
5. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^0(V). By the integral identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero, R.action(ω) = ∫_G mult(p)·orient(p)(ω(p)) dH⁰ = Σ_{p∈G} mult(p)·s(p)⟨ω(p)⟩. On G the indicators equal their defining functions, so this is Σ_{p∈G} |m(p)|·sign(m(p))⟨ω(p)⟩ = Σ_{p∈G} m(p)⟨ω(p)⟩ (Int.sign_mul_natAbs). By step 2 this is S(ω). So R represents S, and S is integer multiplicity. ∎
